'Local authority enforcement' (0) relies only on describing Trading Standards' existing statutory duties under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, not evidence that this delivery route works. 'Strengthened enforcement architecture' (1) draws on the comparable NTSEAT/Estate Agent Act model and existing penalty figures (£5,000; £30,000 under the Housing and Planning Act 2016) to justify possible new enforcement tools, but these appear in prose with empty <references> and <links>, so they cannot be traced to a source. 'Tenant empowerment and education' (0) is pure assertion and risk-reasoning, e.g. 'tenants may feel that they are not able to challenge an agent', with no supporting data. 'Defining permitted charges and deposit arrangements' (1) offers the uncited trend claim 'Deposit levels have been increasing' as grounds for exploring a cap, but no source is named. The mean of 0, 1, 0, 1 is 0.5, which rounds down to 0. The strongest counter-example is the NTSEAT description, which is detailed and functionally analogous evidence, but its lack of any citation keeps it from reaching level 2. To reach level 1 overall the document would need to show how Trading Standards' current enforcement has performed and why tenant education changes behaviour; to reach level 2 it would need to properly cite the NTSEAT comparison, penalty data and deposit trend so readers could verify them.
